newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sacks mining official who handled Busang.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sacks mining official who handled Busang.

text.p: Indonesia's top mining official was replaced on Monday, but Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said the move was not linked to his handling of the controversial Busang gold find.

Kuntoro Mangkusubroto, the director-general for mines and widely respected in mining circles, had played a key administrative role during and after the discovery of the Busang deposit by Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd.
His removal, along with that of the director-general of electricity and energy development, Zuhal, was based on a decree signed by President Suharto on Wednesday.

"The changes are routine," Sudjana told a news conference at the ministry after a brief ceremony where Kuntoro's "honourable" termination of service was formally announced and his replacement, Adjat Sudradjat, the former director-general of geology and mining resources, appointed.
Zuhal was replaced by Endro Utomo Notodisuryo, the former director of energy development.
Kuntoro said his removal was "normal." Asked by reporters whether the move was linked to the Busang property, in which the government has a 10 percent stake, he said: "Ask the minister."
"Government officials can be appointed and can be re-assigned," he said. "There's nothing special."

Industry sources said it was not immediately clear if Kuntoro was removed from office because of his handling of the Busang property or if it was due to widely-rumoured differences between Sudjana and his predecessor at the ministry.

The sources said Kuntoro left his teaching job at the Institute of Technology Bandung (ITB) to join the ministry in the 1980s when it was headed by Ginanjar Kartasasmita, currently national development planning minister.

"Kuntoro is well respected in the mining community, both locally and internationally," one industry source said. "His powers had already been trimmed when the minister (Sudjana) took over his authority of approving contracts of work last year."
Local newspapers have said Kuntoro's dismissal could be linked to politics or his handling of the Busang saga.
The Media Indonesia daily said the sacking could be related to rivalries between a group of technocrats who once taught at the ITB and those loyal to Sudjana, a retired general.
Sudjana said the changes were not due to politics, but that it was part of the outgoing officials' "tour of duty".
He said the shake-up was approved by Suharto after considering advice from a national body headed by the vice- president and whose members comprise several cabinet ministers.
"So the decision is not based purely on the intentions and proposals of the ministry," he said. "So it must not be made use of for political consumption." He did not elaborate.
Sudjana also said he had sent a team to the Busang property to evaluate the amount of gold in the deposit, and added that the results would be known next month.
Bre-X said last month the Busang property might hold less than the 71 million ounces of gold it had earlier declared. The original amount would make it the gold find of the century.

After Bre-X announced the amount of gold in the Busang deposit might have been overstated, Kuntoro put on hold the company's applications for contracts of work, which are crucial to further explore and develop the find.

Industry sources said last week independent drilling tests of Indonesia's Busang gold property are likely to be flown to Australia for analysis by mid-April with the results available by the end of the month.
